chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī al-Jārūd, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who dies: should his nails be trimmed, his armpit hair plucked, or his pubic hair shaved if his illness had been prolonged? He said: “No.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, said: The ghusl of a woman is like the ghusl of a man, and her shrouds are like his shrouds. It is recommended that a woman be given two additional cloths in the kafan, and they are two wrapping cloths, or one wrapping cloth and a patterned covering.

As for what indicates that the ghusl of a woman is like the ghusl of a man, it is the report that we narrated earlier from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd Allāh al-Kāhilī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, and he mentioned the manner of washing the deceased, until he said at the end of the hadith: “And likewise is the ghusl of the woman.”
ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on grooming and shrouding the deceased in Shiʿi fiqh?
ai.summary: This passage gives a legal ruling concerning preparation of the deceased, stating that nails are not trimmed and body hair is not removed after death, even if illness had been prolonged. It also states that the ghusl and kafan of a woman follow the same basis as that of a man, with the recommendation of adding two extra cloths to her shroud.
